requirement.title: trust monotonicity and invariants hold across reachable states
requirement.text: Trust math adheres to monotonicity and invariant properties verified through deterministic property-based and model-based tests. The Wilson score interval lower bound must be monotonically non-decreasing with respect to successes for fixed trials; successes must never decrease trust, and failures must never increase trust. Random reachable state exploration must verify trust values remain within $[0, 1]$, unguarded entities remain capped below their ceiling, terminal lifecycle states score 0, and no entity can reach `trusted` status without an automated guard passing.

claims.expression: bounds and invariants hold for every reachable state in medha-core/src/__tests__/properties.test.ts

requirement.title: versioned store snapshots and migration framework
requirement.text: Store snapshots must be explicitly versioned and supported by an ordered migration pipeline across both TypeScript and Rust. Ingestion and restoration must parse explicit format versions (`sutras.medha/vN`, `sutras.sage/vN`), detect unversioned legacy snapshots (v0), and execute sequentially registered migration steps to bring store state up to the current schema version without loss of episodes or entities.

requirement.title: differential TS and Rust engine parity
requirement.text: TypeScript and Rust engines must execute equivalent state operations with identical outcomes. Seeded operation scripts must verify that given identical inputs, both engines agree on accepted vs. rejected operations, can cross-read stored episode logs from each other, and compute equivalent entity states and trust hints at any given evaluation timestamp.

requirement.title: Rust engine respects per-kind registries and threshold specifications
requirement.text: The Rust store folding and hint calculations must read `registries.kindSpecs` from `.medha/config.json` rather than falling back unconditionally to default thresholds and recency parameters. Custom per-kind thresholds, recency half-life, signal-value weighting, and signal limits must produce identical trust scores and lifecycle statuses in both TypeScript and Rust runtimes.

requirement.title: signal retraction restores post-retraction weight and EMA continuity
requirement.text: Retracting a signal episode (`retract --seq N`) must either recompute subsequent episode weights and EMA $\mu$ values to eliminate pre-retraction influence on downward drift quarantine, or document and enforce consistent 'counts-only' semantics between TypeScript and Rust across log replays.

requirement.title: Rust and TypeScript CLI commands and JSON output parity
requirement.text: The Rust CLI must provide parity with the TypeScript CLI for programmatic consumption (`--json`). Output schemas (field names and camelCase conventions), list sorting order (trust score descending), and command surfaces (`retract`, `define`, `decision`, `maintain`, `mcp config`, `ui`, `report`) must match reference TypeScript behavior or be explicitly specified as a distinct CLI subset.

requirement.title: maintenance plane sweep rules, compaction, and audit logging
requirement.text: The maintenance plane in Rust must match TypeScript's §8 specifications: session-start sweep must enforce downward-drift quarantine and retention-based archival/purging; compaction must fold episodes older than a cutoff into baseline states with in-memory bake-and-verify fold equivalence before executing log replacement; hard episode removals must record audit entries (`audit:removedEpisodes`); and incoming sync/pull replaces must be validated against registered KindSpecs prior to log replacement.

requirement.title: decision tree representation and branch evidence folding
requirement.text: Decision tree branches and evidence folding must be consistent between TypeScript and Rust. Decision episodes targeting nonexistent entities or invalid branches must be handled predictably, and branch evidence must incorporate kind-weighted evidence rather than unweighted counters.

requirement.title: the TypeScript CLI suite passes against the Rust binary
requirement.text:
`MEDHA_CLI_BINARY=<rust medha> bun test cli/src` passes, and a package script runs it so the gate
can be re-run and wired into CI.

requirement.title: human output matches the TypeScript CLI
requirement.text:
Statuses print lowercase everywhere (`probation`, not `Probation`). `show` prints the ema/baseline
line, `clears:`, typed recent episodes with ISO times, and provenance. `propose` says whether it was
promoted and why. `explain-threshold`, `pack`, `status`, `list` and `drift` use the TypeScript
layout. Errors print `error: <message>` plus `(CODE)`, and as a JSON error object under `--json`.

requirement.title: --json output has the TypeScript shapes
requirement.text:
Every command's `--json` output has the keys and casing of the TypeScript CLI (for example `record`
returns `home`, `key`, `signal`, `recorded` and a hint with `trustScore`, `components`, `evidence`,
`temporal`, `clearsThreshold`), so hooks and scripts can switch binaries without changes.

requirement.title: flags and argument validation match
requirement.text:
`record --case-id`, `guard --ensure`, and every other flag the TypeScript CLI accepts exist in Rust.
Invalid values are rejected the same way: an empty `--id`, a negative `--budget`, an unknown signal,
a case id that is not a branch of the entity.

requirement.title: init scaffolds and reports like the TypeScript CLI
requirement.text:
`init` writes `.medha/.gitignore` and `.medha/README.md`, keeps the agent section in AGENTS.md /
CLAUDE.md, validates `--config` strictly, honours `--backend`, `--namespace`, `--recreate` and
`--backup`, and reports backend, store, config, preflight and the files it wrote (text and JSON).

requirement.title: remaining command groups match
requirement.text:
`maintain`, `mcp config`, `decision` / `define`, `updater`, `keys`, `sync`, `--help` groups and the
namespace-scoped home behave as the TypeScript CLI does.

requirement.title: the Rust engine signs episodes
requirement.text:
The two remaining `medha keys` cases need episode signing in the Rust engine: in `require` mode a
write is signed with the home's key and an author other than the key's principal is refused,
legacy (unsigned) episodes count only after `keys adopt`, rotation keeps past episodes valid and
deletes the old private key, and revocation disowns a key's episodes. Today every Rust write
stores `sig: None`; `crates/medha-cli/src/keys.rs` manages keys but nothing signs with them.

requirement.title: help lists distill and styles on a terminal
requirement.text:
`medha --help` lists every command the TypeScript CLI has, `distill` included (the Rust CLI has no
`distill` command yet, though the MCP `distill_trajectory` tool exists), and adds bold section
headings only when stdout is a terminal.
